undetectable.repo_name: comes from the destination directory or the git remote, not a file marker
undetectable.repo_description: free prose; nothing in a tree states what a project is for
undetectable.author_name: the template's own defaults already name the maintainer, and a git config read would be a guess
undetectable.author_email: same as author_name; not stated by any tracked file
undetectable.github_username: read from the git remote, which is absent in a fresh clone's sibling directory
undetectable.license_type: LICENSE holds the resolved text, not an identifier, so MIT and ISC cannot be told apart reliably
undetectable.copyright_year: the year in LICENSE is the adopter's provenance, not a property of the tree; an adopted project's first year cannot be inferred from file mtimes
undetectable.tofu_context: app and org layouts share the same filenames; only intent distinguishes them
undetectable.go_scaffolding: application and tooling share go.mod; cmd/ presence is a weak proxy and the wrong default is costly
undetectable.go_module_path: written in go.mod, but reading it back is ambiguous once go_module_path has been rewritten
undetectable.dotnet_namespace: derived from the .csproj filename only when one csproj exists, and the derivation is already the template's default
undetectable.python_scaffolding: application and tooling both carry pyproject.toml; src/ presence is not decisive
undetectable.node_package_manager: lockfile presence is decisive only when a lockfile is committed, which is not guaranteed
undetectable.node_runtime: package.json does not record which runtime executes it
undetectable.node_purpose: application, library and plugin share a manifest shape; only the exports intent separates them
undetectable.node_build: detectable only from devDependencies, which an adopter may not have installed yet
undetectable.node_lint: biome.json presence indicates biome, but its absence does not imply deno
undetectable.node_subpath_exports: the manifest records current exports, not which of them the adopter wants maintained
undetectable.node_package_scope: the scope is in the existing name, but a scoped name is the adopter's publication identity and reading it back would pin the template to their registry
undetectable.node_peer_dependencies: a peer block in an existing manifest is the adopter's, and copying it would assert a relationship the template cannot verify
undetectable.use_commitizen: leaves no tracked file that distinguishes it from other pre-commit tooling
undetectable.use_prereg: policy choice with no filesystem trace; the default false is the safe answer
undetectable.fork_upstream: the upstream remote is git config, absent from a directory copied without it
undetectable.fork_upstream_branch: follows fork_upstream and has no marker of its own
undetectable.codeowners_maintainers: CODEOWNERS records handles, but not which of them are maintainers versus reviewers
undetectable.codeowners_frontend: a CODEOWNERS entry exists only after generation, so adopting cannot read it back
undetectable.go_toolchain: go.mod's toolchain line pins a compiler the template cannot infer from the tree; an existing line is the adopter's decision about their own CI
